newsitem.title: NORWAY: Mobil has big oil plans in Norway - report.
newsitem.headline: Mobil has big oil plans in Norway - report.

text.p: U.S. oil company Mobil Corp has defined the Norwegian continental shelf (NCS) as one of seven most interesting areas for hydrocarbon development and plans to invest 10 billion crowns in the area in the next five years, the financial daily Dagens Naeringsliv (DN) said on Wednesday.

"This means that the company is once again in an active phase in Norway," DN quoted Thore Moerch, financial director in Mobil Exploration Norway, as saying. "We have not invested in new field development on the Norwegian shelf since Statfjord and Oseberg."
Moerch said a large part of the investment would go to the development of Aasgard and Njord, and the Norsk Hydro operated Fram prospect, which lies in the North Sea north of the Troll field.
Mobil holds 7.35 percent in Aasgard, 20 percent in Njord and 25 percent in Fram.

The company invested 1.2 billion crowns last year in Njord and Aasgard. Its exploration costs in 1996 amounted to 410 million crowns against an expected budget of 300 to 400 million crowns per year up to 2000, DN said.

In Norway's 15th licensing round Mobil was awarded shares in five licences, two of which as operator. The company now holds operatorship for five licences in Norwegian waters and is involved in three exploration applications in the Barents region, DN said.
